title: Latency & Error Budget Crosswalk — Product Stakes and Ops Sprint Plan (2026)
content:
OVERVIEW:
A focused cross-functional plan to align product, platform, and SRE on latency and error-budget rules for core text-generation and embeddings endpoints. Primary goal: translate product-level customer stakes into operational SLOs and an actionable sprint cadence that reduces tail latency and prevents repeated burn of error budget during peak promos and model rollouts.

Audience:
- Product leads (hosted-api, dedicated)
- Platform & serving runtime engineers
- SRE / Oncall
- Solutions engineering (customer impact)

High-level objectives:
1) Create clear mapping from product impact (customer-facing latency tiers) -> specific SLO numeric targets and associated error-budget policies.
2) Define monitoring and alerting thresholds that surface real customer pain before budget is exhausted.
3) Establish a 6-week sprint pattern for rapid mitigations, plus a longer runway for kernel/compilation fixes.
4) Create decision rules for rollbacks/canaries during model and infra changes.

Scope (what's in/out):
- In: text generation public API endpoints, embeddings batch endpoints, realtime chat routes used by >95% traffic.
- Out: internal admin APIs, low-volume batch training jobs, dedicated customer private VPC networks (follow separate plan).

Key definitions (working):
- Latency SLO types: p50, p95, p99 measured on server-side request-to-first-token and full-response time.
- Availability SLO: % of successful 2xx responses (excluding client errors) over a 30d rolling window.
- Error budget: 1 - SLO (how much failure we tolerate before mitigation).

Proposed SLOs (initial proposals, to be validated with product):
- Core text-gen endpoint: availability 99.95% (30d), latency p95 < 300ms for short completions (<128 tokens), p99 < 700ms.
- Chat streaming: availability 99.9% (30d), p95 time-to-first-token < 120ms.
- Embeddings batch: availability 99.9% (30d), median throughput per-queue > 120 req/s per GPU pool during steady state.

Error-budget policies (examples):
- If availability error-budget usage > 25% in 7d: pause non-essential rollout experiments, enable additional capacity (burst), escalate to platform oncall.
- If latency error-budget (p99 tail) > 20% usage in 7d: trigger tail analysis, enable KV caching for hot prefixes, open rollback PR for last model change if correlated.

Measurement & telemetry plan:
- Use existing metrics pipeline: request_latency_ms (histogram), requests_total{status}, model_variant tag, route.
- Dashboards: per-route SLO panels, error-budget burn charts, correlated infra signals (GPU utilization, queue depth, host tail latencies).
- Synthetic checks: add customer-simulated probes on top-10 customer routes (Europe and US) every 30s.

Alerting thresholds (working):
- Paging alerts (oncall):
  - Availability: error-budget burn rate >50% over 24h or instant drop below 99.0% for core-prod endpoints.
  - Latency: sustained p99 > 1s for > 15m for core endpoints AND correlated CPU/GPU/memory pressure.
- Notification-only (Slack/email):
  - Error-budget usage >10% in 7d, p95 drift >20% vs baseline.

Roles & responsibilities (quick matrix):
- Product owner (Sofia Martinez): define customer impact tiers, validate SLO targets, coordinate customer comms.
- Platform lead (Marcus Chen): capacity plays, autoscaling policies, kernel/quantization patches.
- Serving runtime (Liam O'Connor): KV cache improvements, batching tuning, inference path changes.
- SRE (Asha Patel): SLO calculation, alerting rules, synthetic tests, runbook ownership.
- Solutions eng (Priya Desai): customer impact triage, escalation with sales.

Sprint cadence & milestones (6-week cycle):
- Week 0 (planning): refine SLOs with product, finalize measurement queries.
- Week 1-2 (investigate): collect baseline signals, run canary load tests, quick mitigations (config changes, cache config).
- Week 3 (implement): infra/serving fixes, autoscale policy adjustments, synthetic probes rollout.
- Week 4 (verify): run 48h soak under realistic traffic, analyze error-budget burn.
- Week 5 (document + runbook): update runbooks and rollback SOPs, prepare stakeholder update.
- Week 6 (retro + next planning): retro, backlog grooming, next sprint plan.

Quarter roadmap (high level):
- Q1: pilot SLOs on 2 critical routes, baseline dashboards, synthetic checks.
- Q2: expand to top-10 routes, implement automated cache suggestions from Optimize toolkit.
- Q3: integrate rollout policies with canary-based error-budget gating (automatic pause on burn).
- Q4: enterprise packaging of SLO reports for dedicated/private customers.

Acceptance criteria for the pilot:
- SLOs are computed from production metrics with <5% variance vs manual sampling.
- Synthetic probes run in both US/EU and surface consistent signals with production metrics.
- At least one mitigation path exists for each common failure mode (scale-up, rollback, config flip).

Runbook sketches (to be formalized):
- Incident start: check error-budget dashboard -> correlate model_variant -> if correlated, rollback to previous pinned version OR throttle new model traffic.
- If infra resource saturation: trigger platform autoscale policy -> notify SRE lead -> open scaling incident.

Communication plan:
- Weekly status emails to product & execs during pilot (owner: Product).
- Slack channel: #sre-latency-burn for real-time alerts & triage.
- Monthly stakeholder demo of dashboards and recent mitigations.

Risks & mitigations (working list):
- Risk: model change causes subtle p99 increase without obvious capacity signals -> Mitigate: add model_variant tag to all latency metrics and require canary windows with synthetic probes.
- Risk: synthetic probes not representative -> Mitigate: add top-customer workloads to probe mix, rotate payloads.
- Risk: alert fatigue -> Mitigate: tune notification thresholds, add only-high-confidence paging paths.

Open questions / decisions needed:
1) Final SLO targets — Product to sign off by 2026-02-28.
2) Which top-10 routes to include in Q2 expansion? (product to propose list).
3) Agreement on rollback authority — who can pause a rollout? (ops vs product).

Next immediate actions (owner, ETA):
- Product (Sofia): confirm initial SLO numeric targets and top-10 route list — ETA 2026-02-28.
- SRE (Asha): draft SLO calculation queries & create baseline dashboards — ETA 2026-02-18 (in progress).
- Platform (Marcus): prepare temporary burst capacity plan for pilot weeks — ETA 2026-02-20.
- Serving runtime (Liam): spike KV-cache experiment and report expected latency gains — ETA 2026-02-22.

Notes to self / rough fragments:
- Watch for correlated GC spikes in Java workloads during embeddings backfills.
- Consider adding a short-lived 5m SLO window for rapid detection of regressions during canaries.
- Keep product comms simple: "We track service latency and have a policy to pause rollouts if the customer experience is at risk."

References:
- JIRA SRE-789: "SLO pilot for core text-gen"
- PR: infra/pull/456: autoscaler tweak for burst pools
- Confluence 123456: SLO calculation cookbook

End of doc.

-- Asha (draft)
